partial work on issue/2908-batch-lanes · PR #2942 · pinned by `each_batch_step_runs_in_exactly_one_lane`, `a_lane_builds_each_crate_that_it_tests_before_the_tests`, `a_bad_lane_is_refused_by_name`, `a_missing_a_double_a_void_or_a_short_lane_is_red` (14 tests in `lane_split_tests`, `verdict_tests`) · merges when reviewed

The PR has `Refs #2908`, not `Fixes #2908`. This issue stays open after the merge.

Done in PR #2942:
- `cargo xtask gate batch --lane N/M`: a deterministic split, each test step and clippy in exactly one lane. Three lanes get 325, 324 and 324 of the 973 steps.
- Each lane run writes `lane-result.tsv` into its `gate-logs/batch-<stamp>/`.
- `cargo xtask gate-verdict <dir>...`: one verdict with each lane, its runner, its time, its result and the red steps. A lane with no record makes the verdict red.
- The `gate` skill describes the lanes.

Not done, and why:
- `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml` does not use the lanes. My brief does not permit a change in `.github/`. PR #2606 (`needs-maintainer`) changes the `report` job of the same file.
- The `runners` skill text, the macOS runner `m3`, and the treatment of a push during a run. These go with the workflow.

Proposal for the workflow (not applied, not tested):
1. A job `yield` runs `post-merge-skip.sh` one time and gives the output `skipped`.
2. A job `lane` has `needs: yield`, `strategy: { fail-fast: false, matrix: { lane: [1, 2, 3] } }` and `runs-on: [self-hosted, camcraft-post-merge]`. It runs `cargo xtask gate batch --lane ${{ matrix.lane }}/3`. It uploads `gate-logs/` with `if: always()` as `gate-logs-lane-${{ matrix.lane }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}`.
3. A job `report` has `needs: lane` and an `if` that starts with `always()` (the cause of #1611). It downloads the artifacts with `pattern: gate-logs-lane-*`. It runs `cargo xtask gate-verdict <download dir>`. The verdict text is the body for the rolling issue, and the exit code is the status.
4. The triggers and the concurrency group do not change. With one runner the three lane jobs queue. With three runners they run at the same time.
5. Each runner must have its own checkout directory. Two runner services on one machine must not share a `target/`.

Open decisions for the maintainer: the lane count (a fixed 3, or the runner count), and #2606 (merge it first, or let the new `report` job replace it).

in-review removed: PR #2942 merged 14:31Z today as partial work (Refs). The "Done means" needs two lanes at once on one push; what merged is the lane split and one lane. The rest is free for the next claim.

**Offer: more runners for the post-merge lanes** (from mkinney)

Today `wopr` and `uma` carry `camcraft-post-merge`, and only one works at a time because the workflow is one job. Once the lanes run as separate jobs (the rest of this issue), we can add more boxes so the lanes of one push run in parallel:

| Box | CPU threads / RAM | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| dude | 16 / 62 GB | Hetzner, until ~2026-12-12 |
| egg, cheese | 12 / 24 GB each | GMKtec M6 Ultra, Ubuntu |
| skull | 8 / 62 GB | Linux pool host |
| len | 8 / 60 GB | Ubuntu laptop; already has an unprivileged `ghrunner` user (the PR-test runner, currently stopped) |

How each box would be set up (same as len):
- A separate `ghrunner` account with no sudo and no docker group. Its own HOME, cargo home and sccache dir; Rust stable, `xvfb`, Mesa software drivers.
- Registered with `--no-default-labels --labels self-hosted,Linux,X64,camcraft-post-merge`, so it never takes a `cut.yml` (`[self-hosted, linux]`) or `pr-test.yml` job by accident. Tell us if you want a different label.
- Never sleeps, runs as a systemd service.
- While a lane runs, our job pools on that box share the CPU. We lower that box's pool slots so a lane is not starved.

What we need from you:
1. The lane jobs in `post-merge.yml` (matrix over `--lane N/M` plus the collect/verdict job), when you're happy with the design.
2. A registration token per box (Settings -> Actions -> Runners -> New self-hosted runner). Paste the command; mkinney runs the registration on each box as `ghrunner` (agents never handle the token).

We will prepare the `ghrunner` accounts now so registration is one command per box when you are ready.

**Clarified ask (mkinney), replaces the lane proposal above as the first step**

What we want from the post-merge gate:
1. Each push to `main` starts its own run on the next free `camcraft-post-merge` runner.
2. A run always goes to completion. A merge that lands while a run is going starts a **second, independent run** on another free runner. Nothing waits behind another run and nothing is cancelled.
3. A red run names **one** merge, because each run gates exactly one commit.

### Minimal change to `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml`

**1. One concurrency group per commit** (top of the file):

```diff
 concurrency:
-  group: post-merge-${{ github.event_name == 'push' && 'main' || inputs.ref || 'main' }}
+  group: post-merge-${{ inputs.ref || github.sha }}
   cancel-in-progress: false
```

**2. Reports never interleave and an older run never overrides a newer result** (`report` job):

```diff
   report:
     needs: gate
+    concurrency:
+      group: post-merge-report
+      cancel-in-progress: false
     if: ${{ always() && ... (unchanged) }}
     ...
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         with:
           ref: ${{ inputs.ref || github.sha }}
-          fetch-depth: 1
+          fetch-depth: 0          # ancestry check below
           persist-credentials: false
+      - name: Skip a result older than the last report
+        id: order
+        shell: bash
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          SHA: ${{ inputs.ref && inputs.ref != 'main' && inputs.ref || github.sha }}
+        run: |
+          last=$(gh variable get POST_MERGE_LAST_SHA 2>/dev/null || true)
+          if [ -n "$last" ] && [ "$last" != "$SHA" ] && git merge-base --is-ancestor "$SHA" "$last"; then
+            echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+            echo "::notice::$SHA is older than the last reported $last; not reported"
+          fi
       - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
       ...
       - name: Rolling main-is-red issue
+        if: steps.order.outputs.skip != 'true'
         ...
         run: bash .github/scripts/post-merge-report.sh
+      - name: Remember the reported commit
+        if: steps.order.outputs.skip != 'true'
+        shell: bash
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.POST_MERGE_VARS_TOKEN }}   # a token with repo "variables: write"; GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write variables
+        run: gh variable set POST_MERGE_LAST_SHA --body "${{ inputs.ref && inputs.ref != 'main' && inputs.ref || github.sha }}"
```

If you would rather not add a secret, the same marker can live in the rolling issue's body (`<!-- last-sha: ... -->`), read and written by `post-merge-report.sh`; the logic is the same.

The `gate` job does not change: the whole batch tier on one runner, as today.

### Runners
The boxes in the comment above are prepared (`ghrunner` account, no sudo, own sccache port 4227, never sleep). With uma and wopr that is 7 runners. wopr (32 threads, 125 GB) also gets a **second runner, `wopr-2`** (same `ghrunner` account, its own folder and service, sharing wopr's sccache server), so 8 runners and up to 8 merges gated at once; wopr takes about a quarter of the runs and finishes them fastest.

**Tokens:** paste the registration command GitHub shows you (the Windows `config.cmd ... --token ...` line is fine), one per runner: skull, len, egg, cheese, dude and **wopr-2** (6 tokens). mkinney runs the Linux equivalent on each box as `ghrunner`, with `--no-default-labels --labels self-hosted,Linux,X64,camcraft-post-merge`.

Lanes (`--lane N/M`, merged in #2942) can still come later to make each run faster, but they are not needed for "never wait, never cancel".
